# Browserr

> A browser engine for AI agents. One Rust binary built on Servo: no CDP,
> no Chromium, and a small protocol you can audit in an afternoon. The MCP
> server exposes the engine to any MCP client; the engine fails closed, and
> human handoff (passwords, captchas, payments) happens in an optional
> native window, never through the agent.

Browserr drives real pages - navigation, reading, forms, clicks, downloads,
interception - with an evidence trail: every action is logged and every
screenshot is written to disk before the result is returned. Version 0.9.x.

## Docs

- [Install](https://github.com/Omodaka9375/browserr#install): Prebuilt binaries for Windows x64, Linux x64/ARM64, macOS ARM64, Android ARM64 (Termux).
- [Protocol](https://github.com/Omodaka9375/browserr#protocol): The 24-command JSON-lines-over-TCP protocol, every command and event documented.
- [MCP tools](https://github.com/Omodaka9375/browserr#mcp-tools): The 45 tools grouped by job; every tool accepts a named engine session.
- [Platforms](https://github.com/Omodaka9375/browserr#platforms): Asset, headless/native support and requirements per platform.
- [Profiles](https://github.com/Omodaka9375/browserr#profiles): Persistent profiles keep logins and storage across sessions.
- [Security notes](https://github.com/Omodaka9375/browserr#security-notes): The trust model: evidence directory, action log, confirm gates for payments, fail-closed interception.
- [Known limitations](https://github.com/Omodaka9375/browserr#known-limitations): What Browserr does not do yet.
- [Tests](https://github.com/Omodaka9375/browserr#tests): The 45 test files and how to run the suite.
- [Android (Termux)](https://github.com/Omodaka9375/browserr#android-termux): Headless on Android 10+ via pip inside Termux; no APK, no root.

## Optional

- [Terminal client](https://github.com/Omodaka9375/browserr/tree/main/term): Interactive TUI rendering native Sixel/Kitty frames from the same engine.
- [Driver SDK](https://github.com/Omodaka9375/browserr/blob/main/tools/driver.py): The Python client the MCP server and the terminal client are built on.
